correctness.rationale: The full proof normalizes arbitrary derivations using idempotents and the least vertex, proves central representatives are unique modulo scalars, extracts the coefficient \(-2u_{ij}u_{j\ell}\) from \(D^2(e_{jj})\), then deduces \(U^2=0\) and the exact pairwise support criterion via \(Ue_{jk}U\). This yields the order-ideal cut union for all field extensions, with precise reduced-geometry scope. Coordinate rectangles yield all chain components and intersection dimensions; disjoint component addition proves odd-q counts, and a complete six-coordinate equation split proves \(\(n=4\)\) even-q counts. The actual packaged Python checker independently recomputes double commutators on all incidence basis vectors in 15 exhaustive finite cases and matches closed formulas. Experiments are not substituted for the proof. Nonreduced scheme structure is not asserted.

originality.rationale: Primary full-text searches reveal older inner-derivation descriptions (Baclawski, Xiao), maximal abelian Borel rectangular ideals (Panyushev) and a distinct strong-adjoint-nilpotent condition (Hu). Their known results are expressly excluded as claims of novelty. A new coefficient argument proves the converse that each second-iterate-zero derivation belongs to a cut space for arbitrary least-element posets; it also provides a reduced-variety decomposition, all-n odd finite-field counts and the minimal characteristic-two failure. Research-record and web searches used aliases including sandwich elements and absolute zero divisors and compared implications. Priority remains best-knowledge only; indirect coverage by earlier sandwich/abelian-inner-ideal literature is not excluded.
residual_risks: A general previously published theorem about sandwich elements or absolute zero divisors in solvable Lie algebras might imply the cut converse, even without matching terminology or objects.

The old maximal Borel abelian ideal classification covers the rectangle components as Lie ideals; their prior identification and dimensions are not novel, and an unobserved stronger corollary could dominate the chain case.
Some directly related historical upper triangular derivation papers were available only as abstracts, so their full text noncoverage was not claimed.

Earlier December 1972 incidence-algebra primary source lacks a verified day of first public release; the ledger uses the earliest exact dated publicly posted primary preprint among the checked anchor sources, 2002-10-28.

value.rationale: The classification answers the natural homological question which ordinary derivations can serve as differentials \(D^2=0\) on a fundamental class of finite combinatorial algebras. For arbitrary rooted posets it replaces nonlinear second-iterate identities with an intrinsic union of cut spaces. For all chain lengths it computes a nontrivial reducible parameter variety, its dimension, all irreducible components, singular locus, and exact finite-field cardinality. It also identifies a genuinely characteristic-dependent transition at the smallest possible matrix size four, with a precise exceptional count. This is a coordinated structural classification across infinite families, not an arbitrary isolated finite computation or an already known Borel ideal list.
